items.followUp: Write the truth table for the AND operator.

rubric.why: Checks that the OR output is correct for every input combination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the outputs 0, 1, 1, 1 in the corresponding input-row order.

rubric.why: Checks that all possible pairs of binary inputs are included.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for listing all four input combinations.

items.followUp: Prove that x · y = y · x using a truth table.

rubric.why: Checks that both sides give equal results for all four input combinations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing equal outputs for all four combinations.

rubric.why: Checks that the student states the equality established by the truth table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for concluding that OR is commutative.

modelAnswer: | x | y | x + y | y + x |
Therefore, x + y = y + x (commutative law of OR).

items.followUp: Define software sharing and give one example.

rubric.why: Checks that the definition identifies hardware resources shared by network users.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that hardware resources can be shared among users connected to a network.

rubric.why: Checks for a suitable example of shared hardware.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an example such as computers on a network sharing one printer.

modelAnswer: Hardware sharing is the sharing of hardware resources among users connected to a network.
For example, several computers on a network can share one printer.

items.followUp: Define a point-to-point connection and give one example.

rubric.why: Checks that the definition explains that multiple devices share one communication link.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a link shared by two or more devices.

rubric.why: Checks for a suitable example of a multipoint connection.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an example such as a bus network in which devices share a cable.

modelAnswer: A multipoint connection is a communication link shared by two or more devices.
For example, in a bus network, several computers are connected to and share the same cable.

items.followUp: Define bus topology and name the central device used in a star topology.

rubric.why: Checks that the student identifies the central connection point in a star topology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a central device, such as a hub or switch.

rubric.why: Checks that the student describes how computers or nodes connect to the central device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that each computer or node connects to the central device.

modelAnswer: In a star topology, every computer or node is connected to a central device, such as a hub or switch.
All communication between the connected devices passes through this central device.

items.followUp: Define test data and explain normal, invalid and boundary test data.

rubric.why: Checks that test data is defined as input used to test a program and check its results.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining test data as input used to test a program.

rubric.why: Checks the explanation of normal test data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that normal data is valid and within the expected range.

rubric.why: Checks the explanation of invalid test data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that invalid data is outside the allowed conditions and should be rejected or handled.

rubric.why: Checks the explanation of boundary or extreme test data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that boundary data tests values at or near the limits of the valid range.

modelAnswer: Test data is input data used to test a program and check whether it produces the expected results.
Normal test data is valid input within the expected range.
Invalid (erroneous) test data is outside the allowed conditions and should be rejected or handled by the program.
Boundary (extreme) test data tests values at or near the limits of the valid range.
